response.markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure sampled training separation. They cannot establish validation ranking quality. (2) Feedback suggests specific recent interests sometimes matter more than broad associations. It does not establish that greater recency weighting always helps. (3) The adapter exposes the trained model and sequence scoring. Controlled inference interventions are therefore feasible without assuming unavailable attributes.

**Related work.** (1) Measuring Recency Bias [1] warns that excessive recent-item emphasis can reduce accuracy. Recency should be tested rather than prescribed. (2) Petrov et al. [2] motivate history-aware pairwise controls against sequence models. Their results do not establish transfer to these four categories. (3) Krichene–Rendle [3] show sampled evaluation can change model comparisons. Training margins and full-catalog recommendation summaries must remain supplementary to pinned validation HR@10.

### Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal reliance | Sequence scores | Matched suffix/prefix deletion | Sensitivity does not prove intent |
| Transition structure | Training histories | Shrunk recent-transition residual | Co-occurrence does not prove compatibility |
| Ranking reliability | Sampled margins | Paired validation hits and uncertainty | Fixed-candidate uncertainty only |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Controlled temporal audit [1] | 4/7/3 | Originality: explicit controls, established ablations. Potential: reusable evidence, no direct improvement. Difficulty: small probe, position confounding needs care. |
| Shrunk transition residual [2] | 5/8/4 | Originality: diagnostic-linked combination, familiar components. Potential: inexpensive complementary signal, transfer uncertain. Difficulty: sparse counts, score calibration required. |
| Popularity-stratified rank audit [3] | 3/7/3 | Originality: task-specific reporting, standard analysis. Potential: exposes uneven gains, cannot fix them. Difficulty: simple bins, small subgroup samples. |

### Selected idea: shrunk transition residual

At 0% progress, retain SASRec and add one inexpensive, reversible scoring branch. Estimate immediate transitions exclusively from training histories. Shrink each transition probability toward training popularity, then subtract that popularity to isolate source-specific association. This tests whether explicit local transitions complement learned sequence features; it makes no claim to recover purpose, redundancy, or compatibility.

```text
count training transitions C[i,j]; compute training popularity p[j]
q(j|i) = (C[i,j] + tau*p[j]) / (sum_j C[i,j] + tau)
r(i,j) = q(j|i) - p[j]
score(history,j) = SASRec(history,j) + alpha*r(last_item,j)
compare a small preregistered alpha grid, including zero
select using unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10
```

Use fixed training-derived residual scaling per category. Preserve dataset routing, seeds, splits, artifact locations, and predictor-writer parity. Retain both diagnostic interfaces, restore model mode after probes, and return unavailable measurements as null with counts. Use paired category-wise bootstrap intervals descriptively; they exclude search-selection uncertainty. Report temporal interventions separately from model selection.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [2](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Augment each category’s SASRec scores with a popularity-centered, shrunk last-item transition residual, retaining the baseline as the zero-weight setting.
idea.motivation: The supplied qualitative diagnosis suggests overly broad associations can dilute specific recent matches. Training transitions provide a cheap complementary signal, while controlled temporal probes help characterize reliance without asserting that recency reveals genuine intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Compute sparse immediate-transition counts and destination popularity only from training histories. Use q(j|i)=(C[i,j]+tau*p[j])/(C[i,:].sum()+tau), and residual q(j|i)-p[j]. Normalize residual magnitude using a fixed training-derived per-category scale with an epsilon floor. Missing source rows yield zero residual. Select a small prespecified alpha grid including zero through the unchanged macro validation HR@10; count all trials against the shared budget. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four-category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to serialize and load transition counts, smoothing, scale, and weight. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Probe view.model in evaluation mode under no_grad, restore its prior mode, and return metrics plus definitions, observation counts, and nulls for unavailable results. Do not use unavailable metadata, test files, or inferred simulator traits. No performance improvement has been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    fit baseline SASRec using prescribed training data and seeds
    C = sparse immediate-transition counts from training histories
    p = normalized training destination counts
    q(i,j) = (C[i,j] + tau*p[j]) / (row_sum(C,i) + tau)
    residual(i,j) = q(i,j) - p[j]
    scale = fixed_training_derived_scale(residual)
    for alpha in prespecified_grid_including_zero:
        score(history,j) = sasrec_score(history,j) + alpha*residual(last(history),j)/max(scale,epsilon)
        obtain pinned validation hits
select configuration by equal-weight category mean HR@10
write predictor with matching scoring and saved artifacts
run supplementary controlled temporal probes; preserve model mode

originality.positive: Connects an explicit transition residual to architecture-aware temporal diagnostics and a tightly controlled benchmark.
originality.negative: Transition models, shrinkage, and additive recommendation ensembles are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive test of complementary sequence and pairwise signals, with a natural path toward history-aware extensions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions may add little, and observed associations cannot establish purpose, compatibility, or current demand.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sparse counts and an additive inference branch while preserving the trained SASRec architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Residual scaling, efficient catalog scoring, serialization, and predictor parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes a diagnostic metric for recency bias and evidence that excessive recent-item emphasis can hurt accuracy.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal recency weight for the four target datasets.
Perturbation sensitivity alone cannot establish genuine user intent.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling? (Petrov et al., 2026)
contributions: The supplied summary reports strong history-aware pairwise baselines against reproduced SASRec/eSASRec models.
Motivates explicit transition controls alongside sequence encoders.
limitations: The reported Amazon categories differ from the target categories.
Does not directly validate the proposed additive residual.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons, including in expectation.
Supports distinguishing sampled training separation from ranking evaluation.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Does not establish relevance of full-catalog recommendations from logged interactions alone.
